# Mixed Brunn-Minkowski by monotone fiber coupling

## Exact mixed Brunn-Minkowski inequality via monotone fiber coupling

Let d>=1. Let A,B be compact subsets of Z^n x R^d with positive finite
mixed volumes a=vol_MI(A), b=vol_MI(B). Then

  vol_MI(A+B)^(1/d) >= a^(1/d)+b^(1/d).             (MBM)

If A and B lie in the same parity class (p+2Z^n) x R^d, their midpoint
set lies in the mixed lattice, and consequently

  vol_MI((A+B)/2)
     >= ((a^(1/d)+b^(1/d))/2)^d.                   (PMBM)

No convexity of A or B, nor sampled log-concavity, is assumed here. The
compactness assumption can be weakened, but suffices for cap applications.

Proof. Ignore zero-volume fibers. List A's integer fiber coordinates
z_1,...,z_k and B's coordinates w_1,...,w_l in increasing order of a generic
linear functional L that is injective separately on these two finite sets.
Write a_i=vol_d(A_{z_i}) and b_j=vol_d(B_{w_j}). Partition [0,1] into
successive intervals of lengths a_i/a and, separately, into successive
intervals of lengths b_j/b. Let q_ij be the length of the intersection of
the corresponding intervals. Then

  q_ij>=0, sum_ij q_ij=1,
  q_ij<=a_i/a, and q_ij<=b_j/b.

The pairs with q_ij>0 form a monotone chain: as their intersection intervals
are traversed from left to right, neither index decreases and at least one
increases. Thus their coordinates z_i+w_j are all distinct, because their
L-values strictly increase.

For each positive q_ij, the fiber of A+B at z_i+w_j contains
A_{z_i}+B_{w_j}. Ordinary d-dimensional Brunn-Minkowski gives its volume at
least (a_i^(1/d)+b_j^(1/d))^d. The bounds on q_ij imply

  (a_i^(1/d)+b_j^(1/d))^d
     >= q_ij (a^(1/d)+b^(1/d))^d.

Because the selected sum coordinates are distinct, these lower bounds may
be added without double counting. Summing q_ij=1 proves (MBM). For the
midpoint version, all selected midpoint coordinates are integers under the
parity hypothesis, and scaling the continuous fiber coordinates by 1/2
multiplies their volumes by 2^{-d}. This proves (PMBM). QED.

The same monotone-quantile proof works for a finite weighted Minkowski sum:
if lambda_s>0 sum to one, A_s have positive volumes a_s, and every output
integer-coordinate combination sum_s lambda_s z_s is an integer, then

  vol_MI(sum_s lambda_s A_s)
       >= (sum_s lambda_s a_s^(1/d))^d.

A sufficient arithmetic condition is that all A_s use the same residue
class modulo an integer m and every m lambda_s is an integer. Intersect all
normalized cumulative fiber-mass partitions of [0,1]; their positive cells
again give a monotone chain of distinct output coordinates. On each cell
q, every participating fiber volume is at least q a_s, and repeated
Brunn-Minkowski proves the bound after summing q.

For d=0, the separate elementary conclusion is |A+B|>=max{|A|,|B|}; an
injection is obtained by translating the larger set by any point of the
other. No undefined 1/d or gamma_0 convention is needed.

The exponent in (PMBM) is exactly d, not n+d. Thickening integer fibers by
unit cubes and applying ambient Brunn-Minkowski would prove a weaker
n+d-exponent inequality; the monotone quantile coupling removes that loss.
Nevertheless, (PMBM) cannot be applied to different parity classes: their
midpoint need not lie in the mixed lattice. This arithmetic restriction is
explicit and remains essential to any application to the small-cap cover.

## Application to a strict small-cap cover

Suppose open caps U_1,...,U_m cover S=C intersect Lambda, and their closed
versions each have normalized mixed mass tau. Let

  E_I = S intersect intersection_{k notin I} (R^{n+d} minus U_k)

for a nonempty index set I. Its points are covered only by caps indexed by I.
For compact A subset E_I and B subset E_J in the same parity class,
convexity gives (A+B)/2 subset S. Every open cap outside I union J misses the
midpoint set exactly: its defining affine functional is at most its
threshold at both endpoints and hence at the midpoint. The open cover
therefore puts the midpoint set inside the open caps indexed by I union J.
Consequently

  ((vol_MI(A)^(1/d)+vol_MI(B)^(1/d))/2)^d
      <= |I union J| tau vol_MI(S).

No assertion that the midpoint stays in the input parity class is made.
It generally does not.

A stronger, additive version is available when A and B lie in distinct
residue classes r,s modulo 4 that have the same parity. Their midpoint
class modulo 2 is (r+s)/2; it differs from their common input parity because
r and s differ modulo 4. Hence A, B and their midpoint set are pairwise
disjoint. If a=vol_MI(A) and b=vol_MI(B), this gives

  a+b+((a^(1/d)+b^(1/d))/2)^d
      <= |I union J| tau vol_MI(S).               (AP)

This counts volume on the actual mixed lattice, with no assumed closure in
one parity class. It applies equally to I=J and to disjoint cap groups.
